summary: Discovery focused on integration strategy for Brightline's LangChain/LlamaIndex pipelines: evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, gateway/proxy placement, rate limits and quota model, and observability hooks. Customer prioritized compliance (SOC2), low 99th p99 latency for short completions, and on-prem constraints for sensitive datasets. Agreement to run a small dedicated pilot and follow with technical deep dive and benchmark.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Gateway/proxy placement and sidecar vs centralized architecture
Rate limits, quotas, and token accounting

Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference, and with me today are Owen and Leila. quick intro?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Hi, I'm Priya, CTO at Brightline, we build realtime summarization and analytics on customer support transcripts. We're exploring options for serving models at scale and want to understand where Redwood fits.
[00:20] Jonas Miller: Jonas here, platform eng, mainly concerned about latency, cost, and integration with our LangChain pipelines.
[00:30] Owen Patel: Awesome, thanks. high level — we support three deployment modes: Hosted API for quick time-to-value, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated data. today we want to map that to your constraints.
[00:45] Priya Rao: Right, our main things: p99 latency under 300ms for short completions (<256 tokens), data residency for EU, and we have a subset of transcripts that must never leave our VPC. cost is also significant, we need predictable monthly spend.
[00:59] Leila Duarte: quick clarifier — when you say "must never leave VPC" do you mean the model inference needs to run inside customer network entirely, or data just needs to be encrypted/controlled?
[01:10] Samir Kahn: It needs to be internal for those records — on-prem or strict VPC egress restrictions, yes. Non-sensitive workloads could go to hosted.
[01:18] Maya Chen: That's common. so Private or Dedicated with VPC peering are the options. Dedicated gives you isolation on our infrastructure; Private means customer-managed control plane. both support the same SDKs and LangChain adapters.
[01:30] Jonas Miller: How mature are the LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters? Our pipelines rely heavily on LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation.
[01:38] Owen Patel: We have prebuilt adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex, though sometimes naming in logs is slightly off — the binding is there. for RAG we support streaming with prefix/KV cache optimizations; we also expose hooks so your retriever can populate the cache TTLs.
[01:52] Priya Rao: Any examples of running the retriever+generator loop through your gateway vs calling the SDK directly from app servers?
[01:59] Leila Duarte: Yes — two common patterns: 1) Call Redwood SDK from app servers or LangChain runtime directly (simpler), 2) Put a gateway/proxy in front of Redwood for tenant routing, rate limiting, and additional auth. the gateway can be a sidecar in k8s or a central API gateway.
[02:15] Jonas Miller: We were thinking of a lightweight edge proxy for token accounting and to translate the LangChain calls into a canonical call shape. will that cause extra latency?
[02:24] Owen Patel: There's small added tail latency — usually single-digit ms if the proxy is colocated. bigger factor is batching and KV cache hits which can reduce average latency. for p99 you need careful placement; sidecar helps.
[02:35] Samir Kahn: What about quotas? We want per-tenant rate limits and burst capacity control. How does Redwood handle that across Hosted vs Dedicated?
[02:43] Maya Chen: On Hosted we provide per-key rate limits and quotas with throttling and backoff responses. Dedicated gives you per-tenant isolation and you can configure stricter policies; for Private customers you control it via local gateway. we also support usage-based metering exposed in Console.
[02:58] Jonas Miller: Does the Console show token-level breakdowns per route? We need per-customer cost attribution.
[03:04] Leila Duarte: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route and per-model dashboards, token breakdown, latency histograms, and tracing hooks you can connect to your observability stack.
[03:12] Priya Rao: Tracing hooks — do you emit OpenTelemetry spans? we want end-to-end traces across retriever and model calls.
[03:18] Owen Patel: We emit OTLP-compatible spans and can push traces to your collector; we also include token counts and model variant in span attributes. small caveat: some field names in older SDKs are slightly different, we've got a migration doc.
[03:30] Jonas Miller: Good. On the SDKs, language support? Node and Python primarily; Java and Go clients in roadmap?
[03:36] Leila Duarte: Node + Python are first-class with LangChain examples. Java SDK beta and Go are community-supported now; we can share the roadmap.
[03:44] Maya Chen: Quick qual question — what's your timeline to production and budget?
[03:48] Priya Rao: We'd like to run a pilot in 3–4 weeks, production in Q2. budget is TBD but expect a committed spend if results are good.
[03:57] Samir Kahn: Security side — do you have SOC2 Type II, ISO, and can you support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for private deploys?
[04:06] Owen Patel: We are SOC2 certified; for Private deployments we support KMS integrations and can work with HSM via our on-prem package. we'll send the security annex.
[04:15] Priya Rao: For the dedicated pilot, we want to run their LangChain workload with sample data and measure latency and cost. how long does it take to provision dedicated capacity?
[04:24] Maya Chen: We can provision a small dedicated pool in 24–72 hours once contract and payment are in place; for Private (VPC) it's roughly 2–3 weeks depending on network setup.
[04:35] Jonas Miller: Regarding model variants and fallbacks — we sometimes want cheaper quantized variants for low priority tasks. can Redwood routes fallback automatically?
[04:44] Leila Duarte: Yes, Smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants when capacity is constrained, and you can configure priority tiers per route.
[04:51] Priya Rao: On token accounting — do you count tokens the same way as openai? we need to reconcile cost with our current accounting.
[04:58] Owen Patel: Tokenization differences exist across models; we surface token counts but note how the tokenizer maps. we can run a reconciliation exercise in the benchmark.
[05:07] Samir Kahn: Auditing — long term we need immutable audit logs for inference actions for compliance. is that supported?
[05:12] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private have audit log options with retention settings; Hosted has configurable retention. we'll share retention matrix.
[05:20] Jonas Miller: A few practical things — do you support streaming over websockets for real time transcripts?
[05:25] Owen Patel: Streaming via chunked HTTP and websockets are supported; you can stream partial tokens and then emit an end event.
[05:32] Priya Rao: For the gateway we run — do you recommend a sidecar per pod vs a central ingress proxy for our microservice architecture?
[05:40] Leila Duarte: If you need per-tenant throttling and tight latencies, sidecar per pod is ideal. central ingress simplifies ops but may add latency and single point of failure unless you scale it. many customers start with central ingress then migrate to sidecars for critical paths.
[05:55] Jonas Miller: Any gotchas for LlamaIndex integrations? our index sizes vary and we use the index store heavily.
[06:02] Owen Patel: Watch out for KV cache sizing and cold starts; larger indexes can cause larger prefix contexts and memory pressure on GPU. our runtime supports efficient KV cache eviction and continuous batching to mitigate that, but we'll want to tune per workload.
[06:17] Priya Rao: Are there SDK hooks for custom rerankers and latency-based fallbacks?
[06:22] Leila Duarte: Yes, SDK and webhook hooks for reranking; you can chain callbacks in LangChain to call a reranker and then hit Redwood. also supports function/tool calling style outputs if you need structured responses.
[06:35] Maya Chen: Recap — Brightline wants: pilot on Dedicated for RAG pipelines, preserve sensitive data in Private for subset, per-tenant token accounting, OTLP traces, and per-route alerts. we'll send pricing, security docs, and schedule a deep dive to plan the benchmark.
[06:48] Priya Rao: Sounds good. can you also send sample infra diagrams for sidecar vs central gateway?
[06:53] Owen Patel: Yep, Leila will attach diagrams and an example Helm chart for sidecar.
[06:58] Jonas Miller: timeline — we can aim to have sample data and test prompts ready by Feb 6.
[07:03] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else?
[07:06] Samir Kahn: One last — what's your SLA on Dedicated?
[07:09] Leila Duarte: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll share details and the service-level appendix.
[07:15] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and set the deep dive.
[07:18] Priya Rao: Thanks all.
[07:20] End of recording

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mishears (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache in auto-transcript), filler words, and a few speaker label inconsistencies; timestamps are approximate.
